articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.description: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: AI supercharges laser physics with a stunning 250x speed boost
articles.description: Researchers at Stanford, UCLA, and SLAC have developed an AI system that simulates complex laser interactions thousands of times faster than conventional methods. The breakthrough allows scientists to predict how laser pulses behave inside special crystals in just milliseconds, without sacrificing much accuracy. This could dramatically improve the precision and efficiency of powerful X-ray lasers used in cutting-edge scientific research.

articles.title: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy
articles.description: Researchers at Brown University have overcome a major obstacle to creating ultra-low-power computer chips that could help slash the energy demands of AI. Their breakthrough eliminates a long-standing "dead layer" problem that causes promising materials to stop working when made extremely thin. Remarkably, the new technique not only preserves the materials' electrical and magnetic properties at nearly atomic thicknesses but also gives them enhanced magnetic capabilities

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.description: AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.
